answer: To resist Sybil attacks, the network maps identity flow on an atlas graph where nodes stake collateral. Multi-agent audit committees evaluate sparse cuts: if an isolated identity cluster exhibits high internal density with bottleneck connectivity, its reputation hits its nadir. Topological cut verifications detect these clusters and trigger stake slashing. Because escaping detection requires authentic links scaling with network size, the attacker faces superlinear capital costs to maintain the lotus blossom topology of fake identities.
